program:
strings: a guitar's six open strings plucked, each heard by three pitch finders, then all six overdubbed onto a loop, the last undone and redone.
Prior art: the plucked string (Kevin Karplus and Alex Strong, "Digital Synthesis of Plucked-String and Drum Timbres", Computer Music Journal 7(2), 1983).
Prior art: YIN (Alain de Cheveigné and Hideki Kawahara, "YIN, a fundamental frequency estimator for speech and music", JASA 111(4), 2002).
Prior art: the McLeod pitch method (Philip McLeod and Geoff Wyvill, "A Smarter Way to Find Pitch", ICMC 2005), as the tuner example finds it.
Textbook: the noise's linear congruential generator is the C standard's example rand (ISO C, 1989).
r8lsa89do4fbht4j8o8m46glgv: A string plucked at the pitch: length samples of the Karplus-Strong string (Kevin Karplus and Alex Strong, 1983) from a burst of noise drawn from seed.
rf8q0rheb7trb06opnlonmuucb: strings [blocks]: six plucked strings, each heard in so many blocks (8) by three pitch finders, and looped.
rg7riaeqkoibk7cqho3ugvujin: Every string listened to in k blocks, then all six recorded onto a loop of 12000·k samples, the last undone and redone.
utol1bnbv2g8h3rh5duvd4041a: The first lag from lag on (at, with before it and the rest after) whose value is under the threshold and no higher than the next, read between samples off a parabola.
